content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Cloud Armor: Web Application Firewall (WAF) on Google Cloud (GCP)"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Google Cloud Armor is a Web Application Firewall (WAF) service that helps protect your web applications and services from various online threats, such as SQL injection, cross-site scripting (XSS), and distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks. It integrates seamlessly with Google Cloud Load Balancing and provides a robust security layer for your applications."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Key Features of Cloud Armor"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"WAF Protection: Protects against common web application attacks using pre-configured and customizable rules."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"DDoS Protection: Mitigates volumetric and application-layer DDoS attacks."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Custom Rules: Allows you to define custom rules based on various criteria, such as IP addresses, geographic regions, and request headers."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Threat Intelligence: Leverages Google's threat intelligence to identify and block malicious traffic."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Integration with Google Cloud Load Balancing: Seamlessly integrates with Google Cloud Load Balancing for easy deployment and management."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Logging and Monitoring: Provides detailed logs and monitoring metrics to track security events and performance."},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Setting up Cloud Armor"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Here's a step-by-step guide to setting up Cloud Armor for your web application:"},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"1. Enable the Cloud Armor API: Go to the Google Cloud Console, navigate to 'APIs & Services', and enable the 'Cloud Armor API'."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"2. Create a Security Policy: A security policy defines the rules that Cloud Armor will use to protect your application. You can create a security policy using the gcloud command-line tool or the Google Cloud Console."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"gcloud compute security-policies create my-security-policy --description \"My first security policy\""},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"3. Add Rules to the Security Policy: Rules define the conditions under which traffic will be allowed or denied. You can add rules based on various criteria, such as IP addresses, geographic regions, and request headers."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"gcloud compute security-policies rules create 10 --security-policy my-security-policy --description \"Allow traffic from US\" --expression \"origin.region_code == 'US'\" --action allow"},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"gcloud compute security-policies rules create 20 --security-policy my-security-policy --description \"Block traffic from specific IP\" --expression \"origin.ip == '203.0.113.45'\" --action deny --rate-limit-options rate-limit-threshold=10,rate-limit-period-sec=60"},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"4. Attach the Security Policy to a Backend Service: Attach the security policy to the backend service that serves your application. This will enable Cloud Armor to protect your application."},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"gcloud compute backend-services update my-backend-service --security-policy my-security-policy"},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"Advanced Configuration"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"Cloud Armor offers several advanced configuration options to fine-tune your security posture:"},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Custom Protection Rules: Create custom rules using the Cloud Armor custom rules language to match specific attack patterns."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Rate Limiting: Configure rate limiting to protect against brute-force attacks and other types of abuse."},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Threat Intelligence Feeds: Integrate with threat intelligence feeds to automatically block traffic from known malicious sources."},{"order":25,"type":"subheading","text":"Monitoring and Logging"},{"order":26,"type":"paragraph","text":"Cloud Armor provides detailed logs and monitoring metrics to help you track security events and performance. You can use these logs to identify and investigate potential security incidents."},{"order":27,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Access Logs: View detailed access logs to see which requests were allowed or denied by Cloud Armor."},{"order":28,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Security Policy Metrics: Monitor the performance of your security policies to identify potential issues."},{"order":29,"type":"subheading","text":"Example: Blocking a specific User-Agent"},{"order":30,"type":"paragraph","text":"This example demonstrates how to block requests with a specific User-Agent header."},{"order":31,"type":"code","text":"gcloud compute security-policies rules create 30 --security-policy my-security-policy --description \"Block requests with malicious User-Agent\" --expression \"request.headers['user-agent'].contains('BadBot')\" --action deny"},{"order":32,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":33,"type":"paragraph","text":"Cloud Armor is a powerful WAF service that can help you protect your web applications from a wide range of online threats. By following the steps outlined in this tutorial, you can easily set up Cloud Armor and start protecting your applications today."}]
